idea: Adding base to an acid barely changes the pH until the acid is almost used up, then the pH leaps through 7 at the equivalence point.

parameters.name: acid
parameters.why: Typical school laboratory strengths of a strong acid.

parameters.name: base
parameters.why: The same range for the base, so equivalence can come before, at or after 25 mL.

parameters.name: added
parameters.why: One full burette: twice the base needed at equal strengths.

moves: The marked mixture rides along the curve as base is added, and the equivalence line moves with the concentrations; left alone, the base added sweeps back and forth.
steps: Acid in excess: the pH barely moves
